title: Bone and soft-tissue tumours

steps.tx: Benign cortical bone-forming lesions produce intense pain that typically worsens at night. An **osteoid osteoma** measures under 1.5 cm and displays a well-demarcated radiolucent **nidus** surrounded by exuberant fusiform reactive cortical sclerosis, showing dramatic clinical relief following prostaglandin inhibition with aspirin.
steps.say: Benign cortical bone-forming lesions produce intense pain that typically worsens at night. An osteoid osteoma measures under 1.5 centimetres and displays a well-demarcated radiolucent nidus surrounded by exuberant fusiform reactive cortical sclerosis, showing dramatic clinical relief following prostaglandin inhibition with aspirin.

steps.tx: Primary bone malignancies in adolescents arise characteristically at sites of rapid skeletal growth. Conventional intramedullary **osteosarcoma** arises in the metaphysis around the knee, exhibiting cloud-like osteoid matrix mineralization, aggressive bone destruction, and periosteal elevation forming **Codman triangle** and a sunburst pattern.

vis.alt: Radiograph of the distal femur showing aggressive osteosarcoma with cloud-like osteoid matrix and Codman triangle.
vis.caption: Osteosarcoma: dense osteoid matrix, cortical destruction, and Codman triangle (StewardMD).

steps.tx: Small round blue cell tumours present with aggressive bone destruction mimicking acute osteomyelitis. **Ewing sarcoma** develops in the diaphysis or metadiaphysis of long bones in children, demonstrating a permeative moth-eaten osteolytic pattern, multilayered **onion-skin** periosteal reaction, and a disproportionately large soft-tissue mass.

steps.tx: Epiphyseal lesions in young adults aged 20 to 40 after growth plate fusion require careful differentiation. A **giant cell tumour** of bone presents as an eccentric, non-sclerotic purely osteolytic mass abutting the articular subchondral plate around the knee, displaying a **soap-bubble** appearance on plain radiography without matrix calcification.

vis.alt: Radiograph showing an eccentric expansile soap-bubble lytic lesion in the distal femur abutting the articular cortex.
vis.caption: Giant cell tumour: subchondral epiphyseal lytic lesion with soap-bubble appearance (StewardMD).

steps.tx: Expansile pseudotumoural lesions in children contain multiple cavernous blood spaces. An **aneurysmal bone cyst** presents as an eccentric, expansile multiloculated osteolytic lesion with a paper-thin cortical shell, demonstrating characteristic multiple **fluid-fluid levels** on magnetic resonance imaging representing sedimented blood products.

vis.alt: Magnetic resonance imaging showing multilocular cystic lesion with characteristic fluid-fluid levels in an aneurysmal bone cyst.
vis.caption: Aneurysmal bone cyst: multilocular expansion with fluid-fluid sedimentation levels (StewardMD).

steps.tx: Hyaline cartilage lesions display diagnostic mineralization patterns. An **enchondroma** is a benign medullary hyaline cartilage tumour of tubular bones, characterised by well-circumscribed punctate or **rings-and-arcs** calcifications of chondroid matrix, absence of deep endosteal scalloping over 50%, and no soft-tissue mass on radiographs or computed tomography.
steps.say: Hyaline cartilage lesions display diagnostic mineralization patterns. An enchondroma is a benign medullary hyaline cartilage tumour of tubular bones, characterised by well-circumscribed punctate or rings-and-arcs calcifications of chondroid matrix, absence of deep endosteal scalloping over 50%, and no soft-tissue mass on radiographs or computed tomography.

steps.tx: Distinguishing malignant cartilaginous lesions from enchondromas is vital in adult patients. A conventional **chondrosarcoma** exhibits aggressive features including deep **endosteal scalloping** exceeding two-thirds of the cortical thickness, cortical breakthrough, extensive periosteal reaction, and associated soft-tissue extension beyond the bony margins.

right.title: Enchondroma
points: Intact bone cortex without soft-tissue mass

steps.tx: Developmental fibrous cortical lesions are exceptionally common in paediatric patients. A **non-ossifying fibroma** is a benign, eccentric osteolytic lesion located in the metaphysis of growing long bones, featuring a sharply defined **scalloped sclerotic border** that progressively ossifies as skeletal maturity approaches.
